props.title: Stay Tuned

sections.content: Stay Tuned represents a sharp satire of television addiction during cable TV's explosive growth period. John Ritter and Pam Dawber star as a couple sucked into "Hellvision," a demonic satellite service that forces them to survive twisted versions of TV shows. The film cleverly predates similar meta-commentary like Pleasantville (1998) and The Truman Show (1998), using practical effects and stop-motion animation from Will Vinton Studios (known for the California Raisins). A standout sequence features Ritter in a Chuck Jones-styled cartoon segment called "Three Little Pigs," showing how seamlessly the film blends different media formats.

sections.content: The early 1990s saw several films tackling media manipulation and television's growing influence. The Cable Guy (1996) took a darker approach with Jim Carrey as an unhinged cable installer, while Natural Born Killers (1994) savagely attacked media sensationalism. Stay Tuned stands out for its family-friendly approach to similar themes, using comedy and fantasy elements rather than horror or intense drama to explore television's addictive nature. SUBHEAD: Television Satire in Film Evolution

The film's influence can be seen in later works like eXistenZ (1999) and Infinite Jest (1996), which expanded the concept of addictive entertainment to video games and digital media. Stay Tuned particularly shines in its practical effects work, coming at the tail end of the practical effects era before CGI took over in films like Jurassic Park (1993). The movie's blend of live-action and animation techniques would later influence hybrid films like Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988) and Cool World (1992).
